answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent's voting weight to a slowly earned, non-transferable reputation score rather than to account count. A newcomer starts with almost no weight, no matter how many identities it spins up like a zephyr scattering seeds, and weight grows only after verified useful work that peers can mirror-check against public records. Sybil identities cannot buy influence instantly: each must do real work over time, and a misbehaving identity loses its standing, much as a flawed sonnet loses its audience when one line breaks the pattern.
